newsitem.title: UK: Allders to distribute cash, buys stores.
newsitem.headline: Allders to distribute cash, buys stores.

text.p: British stores group Allders Plc said on Sunday it planned to return 50 million pounds to shareholders through a special dividend.
In a statement, the company said it also planned to consolidate its share capital, gave details of a deal to buy eight department stores from Owen Owen Plc, and was upbeat on current trading.
Chief executive Harvey Lipsith said its sales for the 11 months ended August 24 were 6.5 percent ahead of the year earlier on a comparable, like-for-like stores basis.

Allders said it would pay a special dividend of 46 pence per share, subject to tax authorities' approval. The move follows the sale of its duty-free business which left Allders with uncommitted cash resources of more than 100 million pounds.

The company said it intended also to consolidate its share capital on the basis of 15 new shares for every existing 19 shares, and pay a final dividend in due course of 4.6 pence per share on each new share.
It is paying 23.6 million pounds in cash for the stores it is buying from Owen Owen, which include the stores trading as Lewis's in Leeds, northern England, and in Oxford, central England.
The eight stores had operating profit of 291,000 pounds in the year to January 31, 1995 on sales of 76.2 million, and Allders will book the net assets acquired at around 17.6 million pounds.

Commenting on current trading, Lipsith said, "We have continued to experience healthy consumer demand, not only for fashion merchandise but also in light and heavy household merchandise, our traditional areas of strength."
